subject: Persistent MTU fragmentation after private-cutover — multi-team triage
messages:
From: Ops Team NetWave <ops@netwave.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 16:23:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent large-packet drop during private cutover

Sofia,

We started the private-cutover for NetWave Health at ~15:30 PT. After the cutover completed we started seeing steady failures for large-packet uploads (files > 1400 bytes) from a subset of user agents — failures appear as TCP retransmits followed by an application timeout.

Attached is a short pcap (netwave_frag_trace.pcap) captured on our edge right after the problem began. Key observations:
- TCP MSS advertised looks normal.
- We see repeated ICMP "fragmentation needed" from an intermediate hop but many of those ICMPs are not making it back to the origin (or are being dropped).
- Around the same time our NAT appliance started clearing the DF bit on outbound flows for a small percentage of sessions.

This is affecting a small but revenue-critical batch of customers. Can Redwood networking please triage ASAP — we need to know whether this is a Redwood gateway rewrite/NAT issue vs. an upstream cloud egress problem. We can keep the cutover paused if you prefer while we investigate.

Logs and pcap attached.

Aaron Patel
NetWave Ops
[attachment: netwave_frag_trace.pcap (pcap)]

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ops Team NetWave <ops@netwave.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Intermittent large-packet drop during private cutover

Forwarding NetWave's report — they captured a pcap that shows fragmentation-needed ICMPs and a note that their NAT device cleared DF on some flows.

Immediate asks:
1) Can someone validate whether our private gateway (gw-prv-03) is rewriting DF or doing MTU normalization during NAT?
2) Can infra run a tcpdump on gw-prv-03 egress facing NetWave and capture the 3-way handshake + first large data packet so we can see DF behavior end-to-end?
3) Check security group and stateful firewall logs for ICMP drop rules — NetWave reports ICMPs not reaching origin.

I'm attaching the private-cutover-playbook with the standard triage checklist. If this looks like a gateway rewrite we should notify CloudBridge (their edge partner) and consider a temporary MSS clamp on the customer-facing gateway.

Thanks — pushing this to high priority.

Sofia Ivanova
Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
[attachment: private-cutover-playbook.md (text)]

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ops Team NetWave <ops@netwave.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 18:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Intermittent large-packet drop during private cutover

Quick triage notes from the edge team after an initial look (I ran a cursory packet-filter against gw-prv-03 and checked conntrack counts):
- Gateway gw-prv-03 is not intentionally clearing DF in our codepath. NAT translation looks standard.
- Conntrack is under normal load, no recent restarts.
- I see ICMP "fragmentation needed" coming from the next-hop (10.88.3.1) but our gateway is logging some ICMP rate-limiting events — we need the tcpdump Sofia asked for to confirm whether ICMPs are forwarded back to the client.
- Security groups on the private subnet had an overly-restrictive egress policy applied in the cutover template; ICMP type 3/code 4 (fragmentation-needed) was implicitly blocked for a short window — I rolled that rule back at 17:56 PT.

Immediate mitigation suggestions:
- Apply MSS clamp of 1360 on the customer-facing VPC route table / edge (temporary) to reduce fragmentation risk.
- Enable a short packet-capture on gw-prv-03 egress and ask NetWave to reproduce a failing upload while we capture flows.
- If CloudBridge rewrites DF/does NAT offload, we should open a ticket with them.

Dropping a few quick attachments/notes for context.
[attachment: gw-interface-stats.txt (text)]

-Vanessa

From: Aaron Patel <aaron.patel@netwave.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: CloudBridge Support <eng@cloudbridge.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent large-packet drop during private cutover

Thanks Sofia/Vanessa for the fast response. We reproduced a failing upload at 09:25 PT and captured additional logs. Two important findings from our side:
1) The CloudBridge edge (their NAT/egress hop) is clearing the DF bit on packets larger than ~1476 bytes for sessions that match a specific SNAT pool. We've been in contact with CloudBridge and opened CB ticket CB-4821 — they're investigating a NAT offload optimization that mistakenly clears DF for fragmented path signatures.
2) ICMP "fragmentation needed" messages are being sent by the CloudBridge egress, but our origin clients (inside our customers' corporate networks) are not always receiving them — likely because some firewall appliances between CloudBridge and the client block ICMP or drop response fragments.

Temporary mitigation we applied on our side: MSS clamp to 1360 on NetWave's edge (effective 09:35 PT) — we immediately saw a drop in errors for the repro flows.

If Redwood can apply the MSS clamp (or an equivalent workaround) on the private gateway for traffic to NetWave Health while CloudBridge fixes their NAT offload, that should prevent customer impact.

Attaching the cloudbridge-egress.log we mentioned.
[attachment: cloudbridge-egress.log (log)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ops Team NetWave <ops@netwave.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Sep 2026 09:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Persistent MTU fragmentation after private-cutover — multi-team triage

Summary and resolution notes:
- Applied temporary MSS clamp (1360) on the customer-facing private gateway route policy for NetWave Health at 07:42 PT (gw-prv-03).
- Updated security group egress to explicitly allow ICMP type 3/code 4 across the private subnet (rule rolled back earlier during cutover caused partial ICMP blocking).
- Verified end-to-end with NetWave; captured verification pcap (postcutover-verify-20260924.pcap) showing large uploads succeeding and no DF-clear rewrite on our gateway.
- Confirmed CloudBridge ticket CB-4821 is focused on their NAT offload; they plan a patch. We will keep MSS clamp in place until CloudBridge ships the fix and we validate in staging.

Action items (assigned):
- Marissa: add MSS-clamp step to private-cutover-playbook and document the guardrail to check SG egress rules (due 2026-09-27).
- Sofia: coordinate final validation with NetWave and confirm removal timeline once CloudBridge provides a patched image.
- Vanessa: monitor gw-prv-03 conntrack and ICMP logging for 72 hours for regressions.

Closing the immediate customer impact — leaving the thread open until CloudBridge confirms patch.

Karthik Iyer
Network Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
